notes:
Gates and specs teaching for the two player-facing systems in this cycle's scope (shaped patch pieces, boost bays) plus the gridlock strain chip. This replaces the prior cycle's tutorial-agent.json (brief teaching-2026-07-26); that content has already shipped per the repo's git history. Everything below is PLANNED, not TAUGHT: none of these surfaces exist in shipped code yet, so tutorial/ledger.md records the plan with status PLANNED and a real audit is owed once the Orchestrator integrates and teach-sim can actually check it. Full reasoning and tier-by-tier verdicts live in pipeline/gates/tutorial-review.md.

Engine changes needed before these items are literal in code (no design decision, stating directly): (1) content/teaching.ts:37-42's TeachWhen union needs two new members, 'craftReady' (fires true when the pouch holds at least two owned patch pieces whose shapes have a legal union, i.e. the geometric union of their arms is strictly bigger than either input alone; this mirrors the same legality check the craft action itself must enforce) and 'swapOffered' (fires true when the current augment draft includes a BOOST-kind card while the player's owned boost count already equals their current bay cap, so accepting it requires benching one already installed; never true for a CONFIG card, which sits outside the cap). (2) content/teaching.ts:128's patchCellBuy entry and content/teaching.ts:188-193's augmentPoolDry entry both come OUT of MECHANIC_INVENTORY entirely, not converted to a waiver; see tutorial/ledger.md's waiver log for why each is genuinely retired rather than re-explained. (3) The patch-craft moment's anchor ('craft') has no CSS position rule yet (styles.css:2080-2086 defines screen/par/readout/rows/draft/grid/patch only); position is the ux-agent's call per standing practice, referenced via this item's uiSpec (patch-craft-flow, expected from ux-agent this cycle, not yet filed as of this proposal).

Surface budget check (teach-sim's caps): upgrade carries 3 moments after this pass (day-upgrade, night-shop, patch-craft), 2 of them firstSight (day-upgrade, night-shop), at the cap of 2 but not over it; patch-craft is intentionally NOT firstSight so it does not add a third. result carries 3 moments (strain-chip, augment-draft, boost-swap), 1 firstSight. duel is unchanged at 3 moments (par-budget, cascade-bank, patch-cell-use), 0 firstSight, since patchShapes folds into the existing patch-cell-use moment rather than adding a new one. All within the 4-moment / 2-firstSight caps.

Did not file a copy order for the ram tip's CARRY CACHE clause removal, even though the brief's phrasing listed one: tips are self-written by this seat per standing practice (pipeline/gates/tutorial-review.md from teaching-2026-07-26, 'Tips are not routed through copy orders'), and a five-word deletion is exactly the case that practice exists for. Filed five copy orders instead of the brief's five: dropped copy-ram-tip, added copy-boost-swap for the new boost-swap coachmark, which is not in the brief's explicit list but earns one under the standing rule that every new coachmark gets a copy order.

Dependency note: this proposal's patchDrop and gridlockChip waivers, and the patch-cell-use/night-shop/patch-craft moments' uiSpec references, depend on ux-agent items (patch-ghost-preview, patch-craft-flow, darknet-window, pick-to-swap-flow, result-drop-reveal) that the brief assigns to ux-agent but that had not been filed as of this proposal (pipeline/proposals/ux-agent.json on disk is still the prior cycle's file). Narrative-director has already run for this cycle and filed supporting copy this proposal cites directly (pipeline/proposals/narrative-director.json): result-screen-rows (drop naming, gridlockChipLabel), gridlock-endreason, manual-sections (PATCH PIECES, BOOST BAYS), duel-toast-patch-piece.

items.label: Patch pieces roll a fixed shape and orientation; they never rotate in hand
items.rationale: Folded into the existing patch-cell-use coachmark rather than a new moment: same trigger (holdingCells), same surface, same audience. Closed by the patch-cell-use rewrite below.

items.label: Combine two patch pieces into the union of their arms, at night or from the loadout bench
items.rationale: New mechanic, new coachmark. Closed by the patch-craft moment below, gated on the new craftReady trigger so it only fires once the player actually has a legal pair, not on first sight of an empty bench.

items.label: Buying a random patch piece from the darknet, price rising by day
items.rationale: REPLACES patchCellBuy (see the mechanic-waiver-adjacent retirement note in tutorial/ledger.md; patchCellBuy is removed from MECHANIC_INVENTORY outright, not waived). Closed by the night-shop rewrite below.

items.label: Buying an extra boost bay at night, raising the boost cap
items.rationale: Folded into the night-shop rewrite rather than a third coachmark on the upgrade surface, which is already at the 2-firstSight cap (day-upgrade, night-shop). A one-clause pointer here is enough; the deeper consequence of the cap (a full bay forces a swap) is boostSwap's job, taught separately at the moment it actually happens.

items.label: Boost bays cap ownership at 3, buyable up to 5; configs sit outside the cap
items.rationale: Tier 1, a tip, not a coachmark: the cap and buyable ceiling are numbers the player will want to recheck every time they draft a boost or weigh buying a bay, the textbook 'will they want this again' case. Closed by the boostSlots tip below.

items.label: A full boost bay swaps a new BOOST in for one already installed instead of refusing it
items.rationale: Tier 2, a new coachmark: this is a rule that changes what the player does at a specific moment (pick which to bench), not a recurring number, and it only matters the first time it actually happens, which is exactly what the new swapOffered trigger targets. Closed by the boost-swap moment below.

items.label: Post-dive piece rewards, a general drop and the reworked CLEAN RUN bonus

items.waiver: The result screen's drop row names the recovered piece by shape and shows its glyph inline, the only screen this can occur on, the same precedent as the turnCap waiver. Covers both a general post-dive drop and the reworked CLEAN RUN bonus, since both land through the same row: narrative-director's result-screen-rows copy (already filed, pipeline/proposals/narrative-director.json) supplies dropRevealLabel 'PATCH PIECE RECOVERED', the four dropRevealVariants naming straight, elbow, tee, and cross by name, dropRevealCappedVariant for a full pouch, and the rewritten cleanRunBanked/cleanRunCapped strings.
items.expiresIf: the drop row stops naming the shape in visible text, drops the glyph, or a piece ever first appears to the player on a screen other than the result screen without equivalent naming
items.rationale: PROVISIONAL. The naming half is real and already written (narrative-director's copy, cited above); the glyph half is not yet, it depends on ux-agent's forthcoming result-drop-reveal ui-spec (brief-assigned, not yet filed as of this proposal). Filed ui-spec patch-drop-row-naming this cycle to lock the specific acceptance criteria (name plus glyph, both paths) this waiver needs to actually hold. Do not mark this waiver earned in the ledger until both land; tutorial/ledger.md flags it PLANNED for exactly this reason.

items.label: Gridlock wins now chip a flat 6 strain despite paying full rate
items.rationale: firstContact is duel, not result, on the runReset precedent: the fact is first stated on the duel screen's own end overlay the instant the dive ends, before the player ever reaches the result screen.

items.waiver: Two texts carry this, the same shape as the runReset waiver. The duel's own end overlay states the cost the instant it happens (narrative-director's gridlock-endreason copy, already filed: 'Total gridlock. Neither signal can reach the core. The link collapses in your favor, and the dead link bites on the way out.'). The result screen's strain breakdown then itemizes the exact number as its own row, the same way the turn cap already gets its own '-10, hit the turn cap' row.
items.expiresIf: either text stops stating the cost, or the itemized breakdown row (ui-spec gridlock-chip-breakdown) does not land
items.rationale: PROVISIONAL. The end-overlay half is real and already written (narrative-director's copy, cited above); the itemized-row half does not exist in code yet. Filed ui-spec gridlock-chip-breakdown this cycle, which also specs the gridlockWin plumbing needed to render narrative-director's already-filed gridlockChipLabel copy ('link collapsed in gridlock', pipeline/proposals/narrative-director.json, result-screen-rows). Do not mark this waiver earned until that row ships; tutorial/ledger.md flags it PLANNED for exactly this reason. Considered and rejected: a coachmark. The turn cap sets direct precedent for a chip cause living entirely in the itemized row with no coachmark of its own, and gridlock is rare enough (7 of 3800 dives measured last cycle for the sibling turn-cap case) that a one-time rule beats a callout most players will never trigger.

items.control: the boost bay counter on a BOOST draft card, and the boost list in LOADOUT.CFG
items.text: Boost bays hold 3 at once. Buy more at night, up to 5. Configs never count against this cap.
items.tier: 1. The cap and the buyable ceiling are numbers the player will want to recheck every time they draft or consider buying a bay, reference rather than a one-time rule. The consequence of a full bay, a forced swap, gets its own coachmark (boost-swap) instead of living here.

items.control: the RAM readout in the dive dock, and the day board's per turn summary
items.text: Refills every turn. A rotation or a cast costs 1. Up to 2 unspent carries over. The rest is lost.
items.tier: 1, unchanged tier, text-only edit. CARRY CACHE is cut this cycle (ability-agent's four-augment surgery per the brief), so the clause naming its 4-carry exception is no longer true and is removed. The base 2-carry rule is unaffected by the cut and needs no other change. Written directly rather than routed through a copy order; see the top-level notes.

items.title: PATCH PIECE
items.intent: Player is holding a shaped patch piece for the first time this run. State the action (click a slag block in reach, 1 RAM, one use) and the new rule that changes how they should use it: the piece's arms land exactly as held, it never rotates once placed, so the right move is picking a slag block the shape actually fits, not saving it and hoping to turn it later.
items.tier: 2, a coachmark, unchanged tier from the shipped moment. Both facts are rules that change what the player does the moment they first hold a piece (which slag to burn it on), not numbers to re-check later, so a tip is the wrong tier for either half.

items.title: NIGHT SHOP
items.intent: First sight of the closed-day screen. Night patch still buys strain back, unchanged. New: the deterministic 35cr piece buy is gone, replaced by a random draw off the darknet whose price climbs by day, so the player can no longer shop for an exact shape. Also new: an extra boost bay can be bought here at night, raising the boost cap; keep this to one short clause since its own consequence (a full bay swaps) is taught separately the moment it first happens.
items.tier: 2, a coachmark, unchanged tier from the shipped moment. Each purchase button already prints its own live price (tier 0 covers the recurring numbers); what tier 0 cannot say is that the piece buy lost its determinism, a rule that changes how the player plans a purchase, needed once, right when they first see this screen.

items.title: PATCH CRAFT
items.intent: Fires the first time the pouch actually holds a legal craftable pair (a union of two owned pieces' arms strictly bigger than either alone). State that crafting fuses two pieces into that union, free, at night or from the loadout bench, and only works when the result is strictly bigger; both pieces are spent either way.
items.tier: 2, a coachmark. This is a rule, not a number, and it only matters once the player has a real choice in front of them, which is exactly what the craftReady trigger targets instead of firing on first sight of an empty bench with nothing craftable yet.

items.title: AUGMENT DRAFT
items.intent: Line 1 unchanged: clearing a ticket offers three augments, one holds for the run. Line 2 rewrite only: keep the real cadence (three tickets a day, a clean day banks three) but drop the implication that the pool can run dry. With boost bays capped at 3 to 5 and only 4 config augments total, the player can never own more than bays-plus-4 at once, and a full bay swaps instead of blocking, so the well cannot empty the way the old copy's premise implied.
items.tier: 2, unchanged. This coachmark already earned its slot; only its second line's premise needs correcting so it does not go on teaching a fact that stopped being true this cycle.

items.title: BAY FULL
items.intent: Fires the first time a drafted BOOST would exceed the player's current bay cap. State that taking it means benching one already installed, they choose which, and that configs are never affected since they sit outside the bay cap.
items.tier: 2, a coachmark. This is the first moment the pouch behaves differently than every earlier draft the player has seen (a free add becomes a forced choice), a once-needed rule, not a recurring number; the cap number itself is the boostSlots tip's job, not this moment's.

items.spec: Extends the strain breakdown list the prior cycle's strain-chip-breakdown ui-spec already put on ResultScreen (screens.tsx, the kp-chip-breakdown block itemizing rotations over par, traps sprung, and the turn cap). Gridlock wins now chip a flat 6 strain at full pay (BRIEF deep-balance-2026-07-28). Add a fourth conditional line, keyed off a new gridlockWin boolean threaded the same way capWin already is: duel.tsx's DuelFinish interface gains gridlockWin: boolean (true when state.winKind === 'gridlock'); finish() populates it; shop-os.tsx's onFinish passes it through to the duelFinished dispatch; run-reducer.ts's duelFinished RunAction variant and its lastResult object carry it; save.ts's RunState.lastResult shape gains the field. The rendered row uses narrative-director's already-filed gridlockChipLabel copy ('link collapsed in gridlock', pipeline/proposals/narrative-director.json, result-screen-rows item), paired with a -6 value, shown only when r.gridlockWin is true, folded into the same running total that decides whether the 40-cap 'strain billed, capped' line appears.
acceptance: a gridlock win's payout row still reads full rate, never the halved turn-cap rate
a gridlock win's strain breakdown shows its own 'link collapsed in gridlock' line at -6, distinct from over-par, trap, and turn-cap lines
a non-gridlock win never renders the gridlock line
the 40-strain cap's running total includes the gridlock 6 when deciding whether the capped line appears
gridlockWin threads unchanged in value from duel.tsx's finish() through duelFinished into RunState.lastResult, the same path overRotations and trapsFired already take

items.spec: Narrows the acceptance for ux-agent's forthcoming result-drop-reveal ui-spec (brief-assigned, deep-balance-2026-07-28) so the patchDrop mechanic can stay a waiver rather than needing a coachmark, on the turnCap precedent: the payout row already names its own cause inline, the only screen it can occur on. The result screen's drop row must print the piece's shape NAME, not only a glyph or icon, using narrative-director's already-filed copy (pipeline/proposals/narrative-director.json, result-screen-rows: dropRevealLabel 'PATCH PIECE RECOVERED' plus the four dropRevealVariants naming straight, elbow, tee, and cross by name) and render the piece's shape glyph next to it. The same requirement applies to the reworked CLEAN RUN reward path (cleanRunBanked/cleanRunCapped, same copy item), since both are the same underlying patchDrop mechanic under one waiver.
acceptance: any post-dive piece reward names the shape (straight, elbow, tee, or cross) in visible text, not only an icon
the same row also renders the piece's shape glyph
a capped pouch still names the shape that was left on the bench, using the dropRevealCappedVariant / cleanRunCapped copy
no screen other than the result screen is the first place a player learns their pouch grew or a piece was left on the bench
